Logical Reasoning.question: You put three iron nails in three places: one in a cup of tap water, one in a cup of cooking oil, and one in a dry, closed jar. After one week you look at all three nails.

questions.question: Which nail has rusted, and what does rust look like?
questions.answer: The nail in tap water. Rust is a reddish-brown, flaky layer on the iron.

questions.question: Why did the nail in oil not rust?
questions.answer: The oil kept air and water away from the iron, and iron needs both to rust.

questions.question: Is rusting a physical or a chemical change? Give one reason.
questions.answer: A chemical change: a new substance, rust, forms and cannot easily be turned back into iron.

Logical Reasoning.question: You hang a bar magnet from a thread so that it can turn freely, and wait until it stops moving. Then you bring the north pole of a second magnet near each end of the hanging magnet, one end at a time.

questions.question: In which direction does the hanging magnet point when it stops?
questions.answer: North and south: its north pole points towards the north.

questions.question: What happens when the north pole of the second magnet comes near the north pole of the hanging magnet?
What happens when it comes near the south pole? What rule does this show?
questions.answer: They pull together (attract). Unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

Logical Reasoning.question: You stir a spoonful of sugar into a glass of warm water. Then, with your teacher watching, you burn a small piece of paper on a steel plate.

questions.question: What happens to the sugar? Can you get it back, and how?
questions.answer: It dissolves and can no longer be seen. Yes: let the water evaporate and the sugar is left behind.

questions.question: What is left after the paper burns? Can it be made into paper again?
questions.answer: Black ash is left and smoke is given off. It cannot be made into paper again.

questions.question: Which activity shows a chemical change? Give one reason.
questions.answer: Burning the paper: new substances (ash and smoke) form and the change cannot be reversed.

Brief Answers.question: Name the three main jobs of the skeletal system.
Brief Answers.answer: It gives the body its shape and holds it up, it protects soft organs such as the heart and lungs (inside the ribs), and it helps us move together with the muscles.

points.text: gives the body shape and support
protects soft organs, with one example (ribs: heart and lungs; skull: brain)
helps the body move, working with the muscles

Brief Answers.question: Why do we breathe faster after running?
Brief Answers.answer: Running makes our muscles work harder, so they need more oxygen. We breathe faster to take in more oxygen and to get rid of the extra carbon dioxide.

points.text: the muscles work harder
they need more oxygen
faster breathing takes in more oxygen
and removes more carbon dioxide

Brief Answers.question: Write two differences between contagious and non-contagious diseases. Give one example of each.
Brief Answers.answer: A contagious disease is caused by germs and spreads from one person to another, e.g. flu or measles. A non-contagious disease does not spread from person to person, e.g. diabetes.

points.text: contagious: spreads from person to person
non-contagious: does not spread
contagious diseases are caused by germs
a correct contagious example (flu, measles, chickenpox, TB)
a correct non-contagious example (diabetes, heart disease)

Brief Answers.question: What are microorganisms? Write two ways in which they are useful to us.
Brief Answers.answer: Microorganisms are tiny living things that can be seen only with a microscope. Yeast makes bread dough rise, and bacteria turn milk into yoghurt.

points.text: tiny living things seen only with a microscope
one useful job: yeast makes dough rise, bacteria make yoghurt, decomposers, medicines
a second, different useful job

Brief Answers.question: How is a food web different from a food chain?
Brief Answers.answer: A food chain shows one path of who eats whom, e.g. grass → rabbit → fox. A food web is many food chains joined together, so one animal can eat, or be eaten by, more than one living thing.

points.text: food chain: one path of feeding
food web: many food chains joined together
in a web an animal has more than one food or more than one enemy

Brief Answers.question: Write three ways in which polluted water harms living things.
Brief Answers.answer: People who drink it can get diseases such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid. Fish and other water animals die. Crops watered with it are spoiled.

points.text: diseases in people (diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid)
fish and water animals die
a third harm: crops spoiled, or the water is unsafe to use

Brief Answers.question: Sort these into physical and chemical changes: melting butter, burning wood, freezing water, baking a cake, cutting paper.
Brief Answers.answer: Physical: melting butter, freezing water, cutting paper. Chemical: burning wood, baking a cake.

points.text: melting butter: physical
burning wood: chemical
freezing water: physical
baking a cake: chemical
cutting paper: physical

Brief Answers.question: Why can we see our face in a mirror but not in a wooden board?
Brief Answers.answer: A mirror has a very smooth, shiny surface that sends light back evenly, so it forms an image of our face. Wood is rough and dull; it scatters and absorbs light, so no image forms.

points.text: a mirror is smooth and shiny
it reflects light back evenly and forms an image
wood is rough and dull
it scatters or absorbs light, so there is no image

Brief Answers.question: How does the sound of the school bell reach our ears?
Brief Answers.answer: When the bell is struck it vibrates. The vibrations pass to the air around it and travel through the air as sound waves until they reach our ears, where the eardrum vibrates and we hear the sound.

points.text: the bell vibrates
the vibrations travel through the air (sound waves)
they reach the ear
the eardrum vibrates and we hear

Brief Answers.question: Why is it dangerous to touch an electric switch with wet hands?
Brief Answers.answer: Water with dirt and salts in it conducts electricity. With wet hands, current can pass through the water into our body and give us an electric shock.

points.text: water (tap water, sweat) conducts electricity
current can pass into the body
an electric shock or serious injury

Long Question.question: Describe the journey of food through the digestive system, from the mouth to the large intestine. Say what happens in each part.
Long Question.answer: In the mouth the teeth chew the food and saliva softens it. The food pipe carries it to the stomach, which churns it and mixes it with digestive juices. In the small intestine digestion is finished and the useful food passes into the blood. The large intestine takes water from what is left, and the waste leaves the body.

points.text: mouth: teeth chew, saliva softens the food
food pipe carries food to the stomach
stomach churns the food and mixes it with digestive juices
small intestine: digestion finished, food absorbed into the blood
large intestine: water taken back, waste leaves the body

Long Question.question: What causes air pollution? Explain how it affects our health and our surroundings, and suggest three ways to reduce it.
Long Question.answer: Smoke from vehicles, factories and burning rubbish pollutes the air. It causes coughing, asthma and other breathing problems, and smog that harms plants and animals. We can plant trees, walk or use buses instead of cars, and stop burning rubbish.

points.text: two causes: smoke from vehicles, factories, burning rubbish or crops
health: coughing, asthma, breathing problems, sore eyes
surroundings: smog, harm to plants and animals, dirty buildings
three ways to reduce it, 1 each (plant trees, walk or share transport, do not burn rubbish)

Long Question.question: Explain how a shadow is formed. How does the shadow of a flagpole change from morning to noon to evening?
Long Question.answer: Light travels in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks it, a dark area forms behind the object: its shadow. In the morning the Sun is low in the east, so the flagpole's shadow is long and points west. At noon the Sun is high and the shadow is shortest. In the evening the Sun is low in the west and the shadow is long again, pointing east.

points.text: light travels in straight lines
an opaque object blocks the light, leaving a dark area behind it
morning: Sun low in the east, shadow long and pointing west
noon: Sun high, shadow shortest
evening: Sun low in the west, shadow long and pointing east

Long Question.question: What is a magnet? Explain how you can turn an iron nail into a magnet, and write three uses of magnets in daily life.
Long Question.answer: A magnet attracts things made of iron, steel or nickel and has a north and a south pole. Stroke the nail many times with one pole of a magnet, always in the same direction, lifting the magnet away at the end of each stroke; the nail then picks up pins. Magnets are used in compasses, in fridge doors and in cranes that lift scrap iron.

points.text: a magnet attracts iron, steel or nickel
it has a north and a south pole
stroke the nail with one pole of a magnet
many times, in the same direction only
lift the magnet away at the end of each stroke
test: the nail now picks up pins or clips
three uses, 1 each (compass, fridge door, cranes, toys, speakers)

Long Question.question: Explain how electricity flows in a simple circuit made of a cell, a switch, wires and a bulb. What happens when the switch is opened? Why are electric wires covered with plastic?
Long Question.answer: Current flows from the cell, through the wires and the bulb, and back to the cell; the path must be complete, and the bulb lights. Opening the switch makes a gap, so the circuit is broken, the current stops and the bulb goes off. Plastic is an insulator: it does not let current pass, so it protects us from electric shocks.

points.text: current flows from the cell through the wires and bulb and back to the cell
the path must be complete (closed)
the bulb lights when current flows through it
switch opened: a gap breaks the circuit, current stops, the bulb goes off
plastic is an insulator; it does not let current pass
it protects us from electric shocks
